speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have had increasing pain and swelling in your left knee for the past two months. To help me determine the cause, could you describe exactly where the pain is located and if it wakes you up at night?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient reports increasing pain and swelling of the left knee over 2 months. Describes the pain as severe enough to awaken him from sleep on several occasions. States he tried taking ibuprofen with no relief. No family or personal history of significant illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on your age, the chronic nature of the swelling, and the fact that the pain awakens you from sleep and hasn't responded to ibuprofen, this sounds like an inflammatory issue rather than simple osteoarthritis. Given the severity of the symptoms, I need to check your inflammatory markers and look at the joint structure.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Giant Cell Tumor of Bone (GCTB)

The imaging findings of a "soap bubble" lytic lesion in the distal femur of a 24-year-old male are classic for Giant Cell Tumor of Bone. Given the benign appearance on MRI but the aggressive local symptoms, do you have a history of previous trauma to that specific area or any numbness in your foot?
